title: Implement bidirectional sync between CLI SQLite workspaces and MCP PostgreSQL
description:
Implement synchronization capabilities between local CLI SQLite workspaces and MCP PostgreSQL database.

Requirements:
1. Sync Commands:
   - 'knot sync mcp-to-local' - Sync from PostgreSQL to SQLite workspace
   - 'knot sync local-to-mcp' - Sync from SQLite workspace to PostgreSQL
   - 'knot sync status' - Show sync status and differences
   - 'knot sync init' - Initialize sync relationship

2. Sync Strategy:
   - Bidirectional synchronization with conflict resolution
   - Track last sync timestamp per project
   - Handle create, update, and delete operations
   - Preserve task dependencies and hierarchy

3. Conflict Resolution:
   - Last-write-wins with configurable rules
   - Manual conflict resolution prompts
   - Sync logs with detailed change tracking
   - Rollback capability for failed syncs

4. Implementation Components:
   - internal/sync/ - New sync package
   - Sync state tracking in both databases
   - Diff engine to compare data sets
   - Migration engine for applying changes

5. Use Cases:
   - Work locally with SQLite, sync to MCP PostgreSQL
   - Work in MCP server, sync changes back to local workspace
   - Maintain both environments in sync
   - Offline work with later synchronization

Acceptance Criteria:
- All sync commands implemented with proper error handling
- Bidirectional sync maintains data integrity
- Conflict resolution with user-friendly prompts
- Sync performance acceptable for large projects
- Backward compatibility with existing CLI workflows

2. Database Implementation:
   - Create new PostgreSQL repository implementation alongside existing SQLite
   - Implement repository factory pattern to manage multiple repository types
   - Each MCP session bound to specific project context
   - Maintain compatibility with existing Ent schema

3. Session Management:
   - Session lifecycle with PostgreSQL-backed session store
   - Project context binding per session
   - Session timeout and cleanup
   - Thread-safe operations with proper locking

4. Integration Requirements:
   - CLI continues to use local SQLite databases unchanged
   - MCP server uses PostgreSQL for multi-project support

   - Repository abstraction layer supports both backends

Key Components to Implement:
- internal/repository/postgres/ - New PostgreSQL repository implementation
- internal/repository/factory.go - Repository factory for multiple backends
- internal/mcp/session/ - Enhanced session management with PostgreSQL store
- internal/mcp/server.go - MCP server with PostgreSQL integration

Acceptance Criteria:
- PostgreSQL repository implementation with full CRUD operations
- Repository factory supporting both SQLite and PostgreSQL backends
- Session manager with PostgreSQL-backed session storage
- MCP server can handle multiple concurrent sessions
- CLI functionality remains unchanged with local SQLite
- Thread-safety verified with concurrent tests

description:
